executiveSummary: GM0086's 2025 identity, generalized boundary, centre, 30,012 residents, 50 neighbourhoods, 17 BAG places, 33 BRT settlements and eight logical road-border links are internally coherent, and all ten presets execute at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Opsterland combines low managed polders around Nij Beets, Tijnje, Terwispel and Gorredijk with the Alddjip/Koningsdiep and higher wooded terrain around Beetsterzwaag, Wijnjewoude and Bakkeveen. The current Fryslân risk profile classifies Opsterland for polder flooding, rainfall nuisance and nature fire, but not for direct mainland-sea flooding or Rhine/Meuse/IJssel high water. The simulator instead gives the river preset 0.436946 m at T+24 and T+72, and the coastal preset 1.099782 m at T+24, without a selected river, polder, boezem, defence or connected footprint. The river case reports zero affected residents while degrading all services and accumulating 323,875 person-hours by T+72. Pluvial T+24 reports 0.169027 m and 3,000 affected without event rainfall, terrain, sewer, groundwater, receiving-water or pump-control state. A controlled wildfire source at the published Bakkeveen-De Kampen centre leaves that source neighbourhood ninth behind population leaders, despite official nature-fire eligibility. The public snapshot has 494 partial water-control/wastewater points, Liander and Vitens responsibility areas, one grid-planning sample, 76 antenna sites, 23 education locations, no local acute hospital and no local rail station, but none establishes live connectivity, capacity, backup, staffing or restoration. The three A7 boundary records are one physical corridor, and cross-boundary Nij Smellinghe access depends on local roads/A7/N31 or N358 and current passability. The municipality explicitly states there are currently zero emergency support points and only preparation is underway. Exact hazard, service and recovery values must therefore be suppressed or labelled synthetic until governed event geometry and an auditable first-72-hour action/resource ledger exist; zero support points is an administrative fact, while empty, historic, planning and incomplete data remain Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0086 official 2025 identity, neighbourhood, place and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipal/regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK inputs identify GM0086 as Opsterland in Fryslân and Veiligheidsregio Fryslân, and report 30,012 residents, density 134/km², 24.3% aged 65 or older and 4,084 one-person households. The reference point [6.129736540343993,53.056731862163865] lies inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Fifty neighbourhoods in fifteen districts sum to 30,010 residents, two below the municipal control (-0.007%); published households total 12,900 and rounded age-65-plus rows 7,285. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 30,012 without rewriting observations.

Seventeen BAG places have no retained centre outside the generalized boundary. Thirty-three BRT features comprise sixteen buurtschappen, fourteen woonkernen, two gehuchten and one deelkern; labels and descriptive populations are not independent municipal controls.

District heating and public charging are missing in all 50 neighbourhoods; average home value is missing in eight and cars per household in five. Publisher null/suppression remains NoData, not zero. CBS/BRT is CC BY 4.0 and BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2026–2029 municipality profile and water scenarios
evidenceSources.edition: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2026–2029 website and municipality appendix, accessed 3 September 2026; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The current Opsterland page explicitly lists polder flooding, water nuisance, nature fire, cold, heat, drought and electricity, gas, drinking-water, wastewater and communications failure. It does not list direct sea/mainland flooding, major-river flooding or induced earthquake. Inclusion is strategic eligibility and omission is not proof of impossibility or safety.

The municipality appendix describes polders below NAP, nature areas, vulnerable and large-public objects, hazardous facilities/transport/pipelines, possible failure of all vital infrastructure, and national/provincial roads. It is context, not an event footprint or current state.

The official polder scenario is a named mechanism: prolonged rain and wind raise Friese boezem levels, limited discharge precedes one polder-dike breach and an illustrative 0.70 m in that polder, with fewer than 400 affected and fewer than 4,000 involved. These regional scenario values cannot be assigned municipality-wide without the selected polder, defence, connected footprint, arrival and recession.

The regional rainfall scenario describes local streets, fields, cellars and crawl spaces after intense summer or prolonged winter rain. It reports regional illustrative totals rather than an Opsterland raster or current observation.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Current Koningsdiep/Alddjip programme and managed water-system context
evidenceSources.edition: Current programme page inspected 3 September 2026; fifth implementation module planned 2026–2030; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The Alddjip/Koningsdiep runs past Bakkeveen, Wijnjewoude, Ureterp and Beetsterzwaag and discharges toward the Friese boezem. The upper/middle reach uses distinct controlled reaches and a diversion channel; it is not a Rhine, Meuse or IJssel pathway.

The approved fifth module covers Mounleane and Beakendyk first, while Heidehuizen follows after 2030. Measures include changing waterways/weirs, flood-storage depressions, higher stream levels, meanders and drainage to manage effects on adjacent land.

The programme says construction is expected to start in autumn 2026 and proceed stepwise through 2030. Planned work and resident concerns about existing water nuisance do not establish completion, current peil, rainfall, storage, gate/pump operation or incident response.

Koningsdiep-West planning describes the lower reach near Nij Beets/Nieuwe Vaart and relatively low terrain, much below NAP in its scoped area. Planning geography is static context, not a current flood surface.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Partial IMWA water-control and DAMO wastewater registers
evidenceSources.edition: Deployment snapshot retrieved 2026-09-03T01:38:15Z; CC BY-SA 4.0; publisher-variable completeness
supports: Full-resolution polygon containment assigns 494 register points to GM0086: 441 weirs, 31 surface-water pumps, 15 sewer pumps, five sluices and two wastewater-treatment locations.

Only 23 points have a non-null capacity field and 471 do not. The UI does not establish comparable capacity units, connected catchments, control modes, energy/backup, storage, flow, maintenance, crew or incident state.

The snapshot labels rwzi Gorredijk 'gerealiseerd' and rwzi Wijnjewoude 'buiten bedrijf'. These are publisher register states at retrieval, not evidence that the former is processing, the latter's whole catchment is unserved, or either has a specific T+72 consequence.
Point presence and a realized status are official context, never automatic readiness; incomplete coverage never proves that unlisted assets are absent.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Current resilience, emergency-support and climate-adaptation status
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal pages inspected 3 September 2026; emergency-support programme in preparation during 2026; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The municipality explicitly states that there are currently no emergency support points in Opsterland and that locations are being prepared, with a 2026 village dialogue about creating one in each village. This is a source-backed current administrative zero, not evidence that future capacity exists.

The municipality promotes household preparedness for 72 hours and links support points to information and help when food, drinking water or medicines are unavailable. Guidance and intent do not establish household stock, staffed sites, supplies, power, telecom, accessibility or opening triggers.

The adopted environmental vision treats climate adaptation, heavier rain, water nuisance, heat and drought as local issues and points to the Friese Klimaatatlas stress test. It is planning/context evidence, not current weather or a licensed incident raster consumed by the model.

The municipality's 2025 sewer inspection/repair notice covered Ureterp, Tijnje, Nij Beets, Beetsterzwaag, Wijnjewoude, Gorredijk and Lippenhuizen. Historic maintenance does not establish audit-time sewer condition, capacity or storm performance.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Nature-fire eligibility and Bakkeveen/Beetsterzwaag risk-management context
evidenceSources.edition: Current 2026 page and Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2026–2029; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The authority defines higher-risk RIN areas as more than 500 hectares of connected forest, heath, peat, reeds or dunes; Opsterland is included for nature fire in the current risk profile.

Published operational planning has explicitly treated Mandefjild/Bakkeveen and the Beetsterzwaag forests as nature-fire focus areas. This establishes eligibility, not ignition, perimeter, fuel moisture, wind, visitors, access, firewater, crews or suppression progress.

The regional scenario emphasizes fast spread, smoke, difficult sandy access, vulnerable buildings and recreation, with evacuation decisions possible within about two hours. Regional reference casualties/totals are not municipality observations.

A controlled simulator diagnostic at the official Bakkeveen-De Kampen centre is synthetic test evidence only: at T+24 it produces 0.251314 direct fire and 0.447580 smoke, yet Bakkeveen-De Kampen ranks ninth behind larger-population neighbourhoods.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / PDOK, ProRail, OVapi and RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Static multimodal access and cross-boundary acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-light 2026-08-01 and transport snapshot retrieved 2026-09-03, CC0; OVapi schedule 2026-08-30 through 2026-12-12; RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1 published 2026-07-03, CC0
supports: The graph has eight logical links to Heerenveen, Westerkwartier, Smallingerland and Ooststellingwerf across A7, N31, N381, N358, N917 and N392. Three A7 links share physicalCorridorId NWB-road-7 and are one series corridor, never independent capacity.
Distances 0.140–5.035 km and nominal 150/260 values are boundary geometry and scenario-unit ceilings, not route length, lanes, vehicles per hour, evacuation throughput or responder travel time.
No ProRail station lies inside GM0086; 111 GTFS stop areas are scheduled/register context, not live bus operation, accessible vehicles, drivers, fuel, road passability or evacuation capacity.

No acute hospital lies inside GM0086. Nij Smellinghe in Drachten is 4.892 km straight-line from the municipal reference point and reports a 24/7 emergency department, acute obstetrics, eight rooms and 13,398 2025 visits; Frisius MC Heerenveen is 17.398 km. Annual survey and distance do not establish route, acceptance, staffing, occupancy, utilities, oxygen/medicine or surge.

evidenceSources.publisher: Netbeheer Nederland, Stichting Mijn Aansluiting, RDI, DUO, KNMI, RIVM, Rijkswaterstaat and NDW
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Public lifeline planning/register layers and scoped current NoData
evidenceSources.edition: Deployment/public queries retrieved 2–3 September 2026; licences and cadence remain source-specific
supports: A live public responsibility-area query at the municipal centre returns Liander for electricity (record updated 24 March 2026) and gas (17 December 2025), Vitens for water (7 September 2025), and no drainage or media record. Territories are Public Domain provider context, not topology, coverage quality, live service or restoration.

One postcode sample 9244CJ maps to Liander area OS DRACHTEN 10-1i and reports planning fields: withdrawal existing 45 MW, required 63 MW, queue 14.4 MW/20 requests; injection existing 90 MW, required 71 MW, queue 20 MW/29 requests; six projects, earliest 2027. NBNL says this is open planning data but no exact standard licence identifier was found. It is not current load, outage, reserve or a municipal total.

RDI assigns 76 antenna sites (29 mobile, 17 fixed link, 29 amateur, one other-mobile) and DUO assigns 23 education locations. RDI's service states no exact reuse licence; DUO labels CC BY without version. Neither supplies live coverage/backhaul/power nor occupancy/shelter capacity.

The deployment assigns zero local NDW situations, KNMI weather stations, RIVM PM2.5 stations, Waterinfo observations/forecasts and 365-day KNMI seismic events. The nearest weather stations are about 31.3 km away. Fryslân's no-warning record was issued under a 48-hour product, not a T+72 forecast. Empty/no-match is NoData, never open roads, normal local conditions or safety.

identity.summary: GM0086, Opsterland, Fryslân and Veiligheidsregio Fryslân agree across the generated and official 2025 sources.
notes: Feature ID, bundle code/name, province and safety-region membership are coherent.
The reference point lies inside official generalized geometry.
Annual administrative edition, publication/retrieval time, observation/forecast validity and synthetic exercise time remain distinct.

geography.summary: Administrative containment is coherent, but Opsterland's low western polders, managed central waterways and eastern sandy/wooded edge require different hazard mechanisms.
notes: Use full geometry for evidence containment; the generalized boundary and municipal centre are overview controls only.
Nij Beets/Tijnje/Terwispel/Gorredijk polder and boezem paths differ from the Alddjip reaches and Bakkeveen/Beetsterzwaag fire terrain.
Neighbourhood, BAG place, BRT settlement, water-control point and risk-profile scenario are different evidence objects and cannot be collapsed into one scalar.

demography.summary: The 30,012 municipal control and 50 neighbourhood rows reconcile within normal CBS rounding.
notes: Neighbourhood population is 30,010, two below the control (-0.007%); households total 12,900 and rounded age 65+ totals 7,285.
The simulator allocates back to the official municipal control without treating the rounding difference as missing people.
Annual residents omit commuters, care residents/patients/staff, pupils, tourists/recreation users, transit users and responders.

regionalDetail.summary: All 50 neighbourhoods are retained, but partial statistics and within-neighbourhood hazard/service exposure remain unresolved.
notes: District heating and charging are absent in 50/50 rows; average home value is absent in eight, cars per household in five and several household/benefit fields in one.
Published nulls stay NoData; annual age, household, home, business and distance statistics do not provide individual need or event-time presence.
Water, education, antenna and care records have separate coverage and cannot fill demographic or operational gaps.

settlements.summary: Seventeen BAG places and 33 BRT features preserve the distributed village structure without assigning emergency roles.
notes: All retained BAG place centres are inside the generalized 2025 boundary.
BRT types are sixteen buurtschappen, fourteen woonkernen, two gehuchten and one deelkern.
A village, school or ordinary support point is not an emergency support point; the official current count of the latter is zero.

transport.summary: Static A7/N-road and bus context is traceable, but common corridors, local bridges, live passability and care/evacuation throughput are Unknown.
notes: Eight boundary links span six physical route families; the three A7 records are one series corridor and non-additive.
There is no in-boundary ProRail station and 111 scheduled stop areas do not prove incident-time service.
Nij Smellinghe and Frisius access requires event-valid local roads, A7/N31/N358/N381 state, vehicles, acceptance and destination capacity; zero NDW matches is NoData.

emergencyContext.summary: Official planning supports polder, rainfall, fire and lifeline risk, but no live event/resource/action state is selected and current emergency-support capacity is zero.
notes: Regional scenarios and plans establish plausible mechanisms and responsibilities, not current incidents, probabilities or municipal consequences.
The municipal zero emergency-support-point count is a current administrative status; planned village points must not appear available before authorization, staffing and opening.
The 48-hour no-warning product and empty local feeds cannot validate any T+72 all-clear.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets execute at six checkpoints across all eight services for GM0086.
notes: Initial focused audit:model passed one file/two tests in 31.32 seconds, tests 31.09 seconds.
Diagnostic enumeration passed one test in 13.56 seconds; controlled Bakkeveen source test passed separately in 0.77 seconds.
Final focused audit:model passed one file/two tests in 32.94 seconds, tests 32.71 seconds.
Execution coverage is not physical, operational or recovery calibration.

numericalInvariants.summary: Bounds, reconciliation, determinism, service arithmetic and cumulative burden invariants hold.
notes: Availability stays in [0,1], web/core factories agree, repeated runs are exact, demand/delivery reconcile and burden is monotonic.
T+24 values include 0.122075 pluvial, 0.137139 river, 0.334681 coastal and 0.915378 compound severity; six decimals are synthetic precision.
A mathematically valid scenario remains distinct from an observation, forecast, official event, operator state or confirmed action.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Generic major-river/coastal fields and population-led local allocation contradict Opsterland's source-specific polder, drainage and fire geography.
notes: River T+24/T+72 reports 0.436946 m although the authority classifies a different polder/boezem mechanism and does not classify Rhine/Meuse/IJssel high water for Opsterland.

Coastal T+24 reports 1.099782 m and 10,485 affected although Opsterland is absent from the authority's direct mainland-sea scenario list; the real polder pathway requires one selected dike and connected footprint.
Pluvial T+24 reports 0.169027 m and 3,000 affected, led by the most populous Gorredijk and Ureterp neighbourhoods without rain, terrain, sewer, groundwater, polder or water-control state.
A controlled source at Bakkeveen-De Kampen yields 0.251314 fire and 0.447580 smoke but the source neighbourhood ranks ninth, demonstrating that source geography does not govern local consequences.

serviceDependencies.summary: Eight balances calculate, but managed water, utilities, multimodal access, care, communications and supplies lack operational topology/state.
notes: River T+24/T+72 reports zero affected residents yet persists at 0.436946 m, degrades all eight services and grows burden from 79,176 to 323,875 person-hours; the direct/local/service pathway is unsupported.

Compound T+24 availability is power 0.346097, water 0.392466, drainage 0.331568, gas 0.589734, telecom 0.251273, mobility 0.416567, facilities 0.546796 and supply 0.416314; these exact values have no operator validation.

The 494 water points, provider territories, grid sample, 76 antenna sites, 23 schools, roads/stops and annual hospitals do not supply current connectivity, flow/load/quality/control, backup, staff, vehicles, stocks or restoration.
NWB informs Mobility and assumed road-logistics Supply only; it is never electricity, water, drainage, gas, telecom or facility topology.

causalTrace.summary: Synthetic ledgers close, but missing event geometry, local exposure, lifeline state and confirmed actions do not gate consequences.
notes: The model's analytic distance fields explain its generic river/coastal values but cannot establish the authority's distinct polder/boezem mechanism.

No selected input supplies a polder/defence breach, connected footprint, event rainfall, sewer/groundwater/peil/control state, fire perimeter/wind/fuel, cyber target, operator outage or care acceptance.
Official scenario, programme, partial register, annual survey, planning sample, current observation and synthetic model state must retain separate evidence classes and valid times.
Unsupported exact values must render synthetic screening/Unknown; no-match and expired data cannot become zero, normal, open or safe.

recovery72h.summary: T+72 classifications and restoration curves are not governed by Opsterland actions, operator milestones or support capacity.
notes: Storm, pluvial, winter, cyber and earthquake show zero thresholded affected and an operational label at T+72 while cumulative burdens reach 428,929; 124,762; 497,470; 387,624; and 255,015 person-hours and residual service deficits remain.
Coastal depth falls to zero by T+72 while 1,082 remain affected and burden reaches 713,595; the unsourced impact/recovery pathway is not an authority all-clear.
Compound depth remains 0.495373, affected rises 19,137 to 20,853 and burden reaches 1,106,134; all eight services worsen without a confirmed action/resource ledger.
A 72-hour household-preparedness horizon and future emergency-support points are not restoration promises; only valid, authorized and confirmed actions may change recovery.

findings.summary: Official identity, demographic reconciliation, places and settlement membership are coherent.
findings.evidence: E01 confirms GM0086, 30,012 residents, 50 neighbourhoods, 17 BAG places and 33 BRT features; the two-person neighbourhood difference is -0.007% and null fields remain NoData.
findings.action: Retain code/name checks, boundary containment, official controls, source edition/licence, field-level coverage and deterministic reconciliation.

findings.summary: The Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset produces an unsupported direct flood and service burden in Opsterland.
findings.evidence: At T+24 and T+72 the model reports 0.436946 m; affected remains zero while burden rises 79,176 to 323,875 and all services are degraded. E02 classifies polder, not major-river, flooding.
findings.action: Suppress GM0086 direct major-river depth, service transfers and decision-facing consequences. Retain the separate polder/boezem pathway as Unknown until a governed event is selected.

findings.summary: The generic coastal screen replaces Opsterland's authority-defined polder/boezem mechanism.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+24 emits 1.099782 m and 10,485 affected. E02 omits Opsterland from direct mainland-sea flooding but includes a wind/rain/high-boezem polder-dike breach scenario affecting one selected polder.
findings.action: Suppress generic direct coastal consequences and introduce named polder/boezem events requiring source level, discharge condition, defence/polder, breach, connected footprint, depth, arrival, duration and recession.

findings.summary: Exact rain-flood depth and population allocation ignore Opsterland's managed drainage and terrain.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports 0.169027 m and 3,000 affected without event rainfall, terrain, sewer, groundwater, receiving-water, peil or control state; population leaders dominate while 494 water assets remain non-causal.
findings.action: Bind a licensed Friese Klimaatatlas/municipal stress surface and explicit rain event to AHN/BGT/BRO, sewers, polders, Alddjip/boezem, pump/weir/sluice modes and NoData before publishing local depth/affected values.

findings.summary: Wildfire exposure is not source-contained or land-cover aware in the official Opsterland risk areas.
findings.evidence: E06 identifies Bakkeveen and Beetsterzwaag-area nature-fire concern. A controlled Bakkeveen-De Kampen-centre source produces direct fire/smoke but the source neighbourhood ranks ninth behind larger populations.
findings.action: Require source/perimeter, eligible land cover, fuel/moisture, current wind/plume, recreation occupancy, access, firewater, crews and suppression state; otherwise show municipality-level synthetic eligibility with local distribution Unknown.

findings.summary: A dense but partial managed-water/wastewater register is absent from causal drainage and recovery.
findings.evidence: E04 assigns 494 points, including 31 surface pumps, 15 sewer pumps and two RWZIs, but only 23 capacities are non-null and no catchment/control/power/backup/flow state enters the model.
findings.action: Keep register points contextual. Add authority-reviewed catchments, comparable units, flow direction, control mode, energy/backup, maintenance and valid-time operation before any point changes Water or Drainage.

findings.summary: Distributed villages and cross-boundary acute care depend on unverified common corridors and live access.
findings.evidence: E07 verifies one non-additive A7 series corridor, five other route families, no rail station and 111 bus stops. Nij Smellinghe is outside GM0086; distance and annual ED records do not establish route or acceptance.
findings.action: Model event-valid local roads/bridges, A7/N31/N358/N381 common modes, closures, vehicle classes, bus availability, care acceptance/diversion, staff and critical supplies; zero NDW stays NoData.

findings.summary: Public utility, antenna, education and capacity records cannot calibrate the eight operational services.
findings.evidence: E08 identifies Liander/Vitens territories, one grid-planning sample, 76 antennas and 23 schools, but no complete topology, live state, priority, backup, stock, crew or restoration estimate; centre drainage/media queries are empty.
findings.action: Expose publisher/version/time/coverage/licence/evidence class and affectsSimulation=false. Use releasable operator aggregates or transparent synthetic assumptions, with unavailable state explicitly Unknown.

findings.summary: The official current zero emergency-support-point count conflicts with any implied support availability.
findings.evidence: E05 states there are currently no emergency support points and the municipality is preparing locations. Guidance targets 72-hour household resilience but supplies no staffed sites, inventory, opening trigger or distribution capacity.
findings.action: Render zero current support points as an administrative fact and every proposed site as planned. Add an authorized T0–T+72 action/resource ledger for alerting, sites, water, food, medicine, power, sanitation, communications, welfare and mutual aid.

findings.summary: T+72 recovery and current all-clear implications are unsupported by actions and incomplete feeds.
findings.evidence: Several presets show operational/zero affected at T+72 despite residual service deficits and large cumulative burden; compound worsens. E08 has no local NDW/weather/water/air/seismic observations and the warning horizon is only 48 hours.
findings.action: Prevent zero thresholded affected or empty feeds from implying recovery/safety. Require named action owner, trigger, resources, acknowledgement, completion/expiry and unresolved carry-over beyond T+72.

corrections.summary: Suppress GM0086's false Rhine/Meuse/IJssel and generic coastal depth; add source-selected polder/boezem flooding.
corrections.validation: GM0086 direct river/coastal consequences are zero/Unknown across T+0/6/12/24/48/72 unless a governed event supplies named water system, polder/defence, breach, connected footprint, depth, arrival, duration, recession, version/licence and NoData. Polder eligibility alone never generates municipal depth.

corrections.summary: Replace population-led Opsterland local distribution with evidence-gated pluvial and fire geography.
corrections.validation: Unsupported local choropleths render Unknown. Pluvial fixtures bind licensed rainfall/stress, terrain, sewer, groundwater, polders, Alddjip/boezem and controls; a controlled Bakkeveen-De Kampen fire fixture contains the source and uses land cover/fuel/wind rather than population rank.

corrections.summary: Represent Opsterland water-chain and public utility/care registers as contextual evidence without invented operation.
corrections.validation: The 494 partial HWH points, Liander/Vitens territories, NBNL sample, antennas, schools and hospitals show provenance/time/coverage/licence/evidence class. Null capacity and register status never imply current state; no context point changes service without an explicit authorized event binding.

corrections.summary: Make A7 and cross-boundary Opsterland access non-additive, multimodal and validity-bound.
corrections.validation: Three A7 boundary records share one physical ceiling; N-road/local crossings remain separate. Nij Smellinghe/Frisius, evacuation and supply require valid closures, local paths, vehicle/mode capacity and destination acceptance. Empty NDW never means open.

corrections.summary: Add an Unknown-first Opsterland first-72-hour action/resource ledger with exact support-point lifecycle.
corrections.validation: Current support-point count displays zero; proposed village sites remain planned until authorized/open/staffed/supplied. Only confirmed valid actions change recovery, zero affected never yields all-clear with residual/Unknown needs, and unresolved operations carry beyond T+72.

residualLimitations: No authority-selected Opsterland polder/boezem event supplies defence state, breach/overtopping, connected footprint, arrival, depth, duration or recession; direct sea and named-major-river proximity fields are not substitutes.
No complete versioned local rainfall, AHN/soil/groundwater, sewer, culvert, storage, peilgebied, receiving-water, pump/weir/sluice control or road-passability model is consumed.
HWH coverage is partial; 471 of 494 capacity values are null and the remaining values do not establish comparable units, connected catchments, operation, energy/backup, crew or reserve.
No event-valid Bakkeveen/Beetsterzwaag ignition, perimeter, complete combustible cover, fuel moisture, wind/smoke, recreation occupancy, access, firewater, crew or suppression state is consumed.
No operator-approved Liander feeder, Vitens pressure zone, gas, telecom/backhaul, critical-customer, switching, live load/flow/quality, backup, crew or restoration topology is public and consumed.
NWB/GTFS establish geometry and schedule context only; no live local bridge/road/bus status, evacuation vehicle inventory or responder/care travel time is represented.
No live Nij Smellinghe/Frisius acceptance, staffing, occupancy, utilities, backup/fuel, oxygen/blood/medicine, supply or transfer state is represented.
The official current emergency-support-point count is zero; planned locations, ordinary village support points and schools are not shelters or stocked operational sites.
Scenario outputs remain deterministic exercises, not current observations, forecasts, probabilities, casualties, operator commitments or calibrated losses.
provinceReviewFlags: Across Fryslân, separate direct sea/mainland flooding, polder-dike failure, boezem flooding, local stream/canal flooding, rainfall nuisance and Rhine/Meuse/IJssel high water; eligibility never substitutes for a connected footprint.

Build a governed Wetterskip adapter for polder/boezem compartments, defences, Alddjip/Koningsdiep, pumps, weirs, sluices, wastewater and valid-time control while preserving partial coverage and NoData.

Replace common population-led neighbourhood allocation with source-specific rain, fire, wind, heat and cyber geography; retain official Bakkeveen/Beetsterzwaag nature-fire eligibility without inventing an incident.
Treat A7 boundary records as one non-additive series corridor and audit N31/N358/N381/local bridge dependencies for Drachten/Heerenveen care, supply, evacuation and mutual aid.
Keep Liander, Vitens, NBNL, antenna, education, hospital and transport registers contextual until current connectivity, capacity, backup and state are authorized and time-aligned.

Preserve Opsterland's official zero emergency-support-point status and audit the lifecycle of proposed village sites; 72 hours is a preparedness/operations window, never a guaranteed restoration deadline.
